title: Drive it Further With These Easy Steps…

context.format: Driver-speed tutorial with own shot progression and result cards
context.style: Four movement ideas, then controlled and maximum effort; progressively warming up

coverage.visual_review_method: 20 overview, 54 detail, 39 sequence and nine result-check frames across 12 contact sheets, all inspected. Source annotations and stable result cards checked. Sampled visual review across 9:50, not continuous playback.
limitations: 480p source and edited replays; no calibrated pose or instrument export.
Result-card animations contain transient digits; only settled values used.
No student diagnosis or measured long-term training improvement.

evidence.attribution: Ryan Ruffels explaining and demonstrating his own driver-speed work
evidence.session: Single driver session, progressively increasing effort
evidence.summary: Ruffels wants a longer speed swing created through torso and hip turn rather than arms dragging independently. Hands, arms and body start takeaway together. Longer backswing is presented as more time/stretch. Source cards support body turn and length.
limitations: No measured hip/torso angle, stretch or segment timing. More turn/length is a speed option, not a universal cure.

evidence.attribution: Ryan Ruffels explaining and demonstrating his own driver-speed work
evidence.session: Single driver session, progressively increasing effort
evidence.summary: He contrasts tensing forearms and gripping hard when trying for speed with a very soft loose hold. Almost letting club fall out is his exaggerated feel for allowing lag; later he clarifies hands support club and do not death-grip it.
limitations: No grip-force measure or proof more lag always means more speed. Maintain control of club; do not prescribe literal loss of grip.

evidence.attribution: Ryan Ruffels explaining and demonstrating his own driver-speed work
evidence.session: Single driver session, progressively increasing effort
evidence.summary: Ruffels describes his own high-effort tendency: lead arm moves off chest and hands travel far out, with unstable face by his account. He wants lead-upper-arm/chest connection while rotating.

frames.observation: Points to lead upper arm/chest relationship.

limitations: Personal tendency rather than diagnosis of all golfers. Later he explicitly says contact is not maintained completely.

evidence.attribution: Ryan Ruffels explaining and demonstrating his own driver-speed work
evidence.session: Single driver session, progressively increasing effort
evidence.summary: First fuller-turn shot is demonstrated, with source circles around torso/pelvis. Result card displays 178 ball speed and 299 carry; he says he is still warming up.
limitations: Source-added circles illustrate movement, not measured rotation. Card is edited source report, not a raw launch-monitor export. Warm-up and effort vary across shots.

evidence.attribution: Ryan Ruffels explaining and demonstrating his own driver-speed work
evidence.session: Single driver session, progressively increasing effort
evidence.summary: Longer than his fairway-finder/normal swing, Ruffels wants driver shaft at least parallel at top, while normally slightly short. Source horizontal/shaft lines illustrate that reference. Card shows 181 ball speed and 315 carry, resolving missing digit in automatic caption.

frames.observation: Source horizontal line at backswing reference.
Horizontal red and shaft yellow lines at top.

limitations: Parallel is this player's speed-swing target, not universal threshold. No calibrated shaft angle. Caption 35 is not used as carry.

evidence.attribution: Ryan Ruffels explaining and demonstrating his own driver-speed work
evidence.session: Single driver session, progressively increasing effort
evidence.summary: He adds softer hands while retaining turn and length, using small steps/waggles to avoid tension. Card shows 184 ball speed and 322 carry.
limitations: One cumulative example cannot isolate grip-pressure effect. No measured force or lag change.

evidence.attribution: Ryan Ruffels explaining and demonstrating his own driver-speed work
evidence.session: Single driver session, progressively increasing effort
evidence.summary: For control at higher effort, he repeats upper-arm/chest connection. He clarifies it will not stay entirely touching; intention brings hand path inward, club outward and stabilizes face by his account. The combined shot card shows 183 ball speed and 323 carry.
limitations: Ball speed decreases from previous 184 despite general faster-through-each-step commentary. No measured face stability or hand-path radius. Do not pin arm rigidly to chest.

evidence.attribution: Ryan Ruffels explaining and demonstrating his own driver-speed work
evidence.session: Single driver session, progressively increasing effort
evidence.summary: Ruffels describes repeated speed work and pushing familiar effort limits over time. He suggests 20–30 hard shots a day as his example and rejects expecting one session to create durable 170-to-180 ball-speed improvement. He distinguishes already-practiced feels from a beginner thinking of all steps.
limitations: Dose is source suggestion, not personalized training program; no recovery, readiness, adherence or longitudinal data. Mental-limit explanation is not independently validated.

evidence.attribution: Ryan Ruffels explaining and demonstrating his own driver-speed work
evidence.session: Single driver session, progressively increasing effort
evidence.summary: Two attempts at the fastest effort he would use on a wide-open course hole are shown. Stable result cards show 186/334 and 186/336. He distinguishes this from a still faster effort where he loses control.
limitations: These are range examples of claimed on-course effort, not actual course outcomes. Transient rolling digits at 448 seconds are graphic animation, not a separate carry result. No dispersion statistic.

evidence.attribution: Ryan Ruffels explaining and demonstrating his own driver-speed work
evidence.session: Single driver session, progressively increasing effort
evidence.summary: Maximum-speed practice uses rocking/long waggles and a moving start. First maximum effort is verbally reported as 189 ball speed and 341 carry. Second displays 190/349. Ruffels acknowledges less strike, direction and spin control. Club speeds are estimates because clubface dots are absent: usual 123–124, course-fast 126–130, maximum about 130–135. Speed and control are trained separately then combined.

frames.observation: Verbal result discussion without numeric card in inspected frame.
Moving setup before second maximum effort.

limitations: 189/341 is spoken; no stable numeric card verified for that attempt. Club-speed estimates are not instrument measurements. Edited carry values lack launch/spin/environment settings. No measured dispersion or lasting gain.

evidence.attribution: Ryan Ruffels explaining and demonstrating his own driver-speed work
evidence.session: Single driver session, progressively increasing effort
evidence.summary: Recap lists bigger turn, longer swing, softer grip and arm/chest connection. This summarizes a practiced sequence, not a reason to send four simultaneous swing thoughts to a learner.
limitations: Source promises of added distance are not a measured user outcome.

cases.title: Create a fuller speed swing through body turn
cases.coaching_finding: Length created by independent arm drag is the general contrast; Ruffels seeks fuller driver turn.
cases.coach_reasoning: Torso and hip rotation provide backswing length while takeaway stays organized.

intervention.cue: Make the fuller turn with hands, arms and body starting together.
intervention.rehearsal: A few practice pumps to feel torso and hips turn.

applicability: Driver-speed objective and golfer can use the added turn effectively.
unknowns: No physical screen or universal turn-angle target.
cases.observed_result: First turn-focused example displays 178 / 299 while warming up.

selection.policy_origin: One focus, at most two compatible cues per user preference. Store full source progression without delivering all four at once.
selection.reassess: Compare speed, strike and control with usual swing before adding length.

cases.title: Test a longer backswing relative to the player's stock swing
cases.coaching_finding: Ruffels normally stops somewhat short of parallel and uses a shorter fairway-finder.
cases.coach_reasoning: More time/length is proposed for the higher-speed task.

intervention.cue: Let the swing become longer through the turn.
intervention.personal_reference: At least parallel is his own driver-speed reference, not a required position for everyone.

applicability: Speed is the selected task and longer swing does not create a harmful loss of usable contact/control.
unknowns: No isolated causal test or validated optimal length.

selection.policy_origin: One focus, at most two compatible cues per user preference. Store full source progression without delivering all four at once.
selection.reassess: Compare repeated outcomes rather than declare one longer shot proves the mechanism.

cases.title: Reduce excessive grip tension while keeping the club supported
cases.coaching_finding: Trying harder can produce tense forearms and an unnecessarily tight hold.
cases.coach_reasoning: Ruffels uses softer hands and moving setup to allow the club to move more freely.

intervention.cue: Keep hands soft while supporting the club.
intervention.routine: Small steps or waggles help him avoid a rigid start.

applicability: Observed tension during speed intent and player retains club control.
unknowns: No numerical grip force or proof that more lag is always beneficial.

selection.policy_origin: One focus, at most two compatible cues per user preference. Store full source progression without delivering all four at once.
selection.reassess: Check grip security, speed and strike rather than seek the loosest possible hold.

cases.title: Use lead-arm/chest connection as a personal control feel
cases.coaching_finding: Ruffels reports lead arm leaving chest and hands moving out when he swings hard, making face less stable.
cases.coach_reasoning: Connection feel is intended to bring hand path inward and organize delivery at higher speed.

intervention.cue: Feel the lead upper arm working with the chest.
intervention.exception: He explicitly permits separation; do not clamp arm to torso throughout swing.

applicability: Similar observed high-effort hand-path/control issue and positive response to trial.
unknowns: No measured face stability, radius or universal arm-contact requirement.
cases.observed_result: Combined attempt shows 183 / 323, not a ball-speed increase over preceding 184.

selection.policy_origin: One focus, at most two compatible cues per user preference. Store full source progression without delivering all four at once.
selection.reassess: Assess strike and dispersion, not only speed or whether arm touches chest.

cases.title: Use controlled high effort only when the course task allows it
cases.coaching_finding: Wide-open hole offers room to use more than stock effort, but maximum effort feels less controllable to Ruffels.
cases.coach_reasoning: He chooses an effort ceiling he believes still permits useful strike and direction.

intervention.action: Select a practiced high-effort swing when landing space and shot objective allow it.
intervention.avoid: Do not use the maximum practice swing merely because it produced the longest carry.

applicability: A golfer has established a usable effort level and the hole offers enough room for its dispersion.
unknowns: No measured safe dispersion envelope or actual course test.
cases.observed_result: Range examples labelled course-fast show 186 / 334 and 186 / 336.

selection.coaching_focus: Choose effort appropriate to the hole
selection.policy_origin: One focus, at most two compatible cues per user preference. Store full source progression without delivering all four at once.
selection.reassess: Track actual strike and dispersion at each effort level.

cases.title: Separate maximum-speed practice from on-course control
cases.coaching_finding: Familiar effort can limit speed practice; at maximum effort Ruffels accepts poorer strike/direction/spin control.
cases.coach_reasoning: Repeated high-intent practice and a moving start are proposed to expand available speed before returning to playable control.

intervention.task: Use a dedicated speed session with rocking/waggles and a non-static start.
intervention.source_dose: Source suggests 20–30 hard shots a day and describes groups of 10–15; not a personalized prescription.
intervention.transfer: Reintroduce strike and direction targets before using the new effort on course.

applicability: Explicit speed-training objective, suitable practice setting and individual readiness.
unknowns: No recovery/adaptation data or guarantee of durable gains; club speeds are estimates.
cases.observed_result: First max reported 189 / 341; second displayed 190 / 349. No longitudinal gain demonstrated.

selection.coaching_focus: Practice higher speed as a separate task
selection.policy_origin: One focus, at most two compatible cues per user preference. Store full source progression without delivering all four at once.
selection.reassess: Measure repeated speed and then verify strike/dispersion before course transfer.

source_ambiguities.issue: Caption 35 carry resolved to stable on-screen 315.
General faster-each-step commentary does not match ball speed decreasing from 184 to 183; preserve displayed sequence.

Final rolling carry settles at 349; transient digits not separate results.

cross_source_links.relation: Longer is conditional on objective and player
cross_source_links.explanation: Brennan’s optional shorter-turn work contrasts with Ruffels’ longer speed swing. Neither establishes one ideal backswing length.

cross_source_links.relation: Secure hold and reduced tension need context
cross_source_links.explanation: Harrington wants hands securely seated with free wrists; Ruffels clarifies soft hands still support the club. Do not equate softness with slipping.

cross_source_links.relation: Lag language is not a universal speed diagnosis
cross_source_links.explanation: Menante’s measured lag/timing pattern differs from Ruffels’ general soft-grip explanation. More lag must not become an automatic target.
Allen’s guarded intent and Ruffels’ selected course-fast effort both show that intended effort matters; the acceptable dispersion still needs player evidence.

within_source_distinctions.relationship: Cumulative progression, not isolated tests and not four simultaneous user cues.
Controlled course effort differs from maximum practice effort with admitted strike/direction losses.

annotation_opportunities: Keep source body-turn circles and parallel reference separate from measured angles.
Pair each result card with its effort stage; do not count replay frames as new shots.
Label club-speed estimates and card animation explicitly.
Show moving setup without prescribing every exaggerated practice movement on course.
excluded_material: Universal speed/distance promises and mental-limit explanation as established science.
Claim of a measured individual contribution from each cue.

independent_validation.reason: Own-player tutorial progression with result cards but no isolated test, individualized assessment or longitudinal outcome.
